title: An AI-ready, data engineering playbook for FAIR Integration in EOSC and beyond: CDIF4EOSC Workshop, London, Friday 9 October, in person registration open
content:
In person registration is open for this informative and interactive workshop about the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) and the CDIF4EOSC project. The workshop is being held as an RDA 27th Plenary Meeting Co-located Event.

Register here to attend in person: https://forms.gle/CSmL6kcxJerWPPuV7
Date: Friday, 9th October 2026
Time: 09:30-16:00 BST
Location: The Long Room, Kia Oval Cricket Ground
Format: In person (hybrid access being explored, but not yet confirmed)

Details: The distinct approach of the CDIF4EOSC project is to build on the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF). The project will extend the CDIF recommendations, adding profiles and guidelines, and use case based examples, to form a comprehensive and actionable playbook for FAIR Integration in the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) and beyond.

title: Webinar: Bringing Data Sovereignty into Participatory Sciences
content:
Wednesday 9 September at 19:00 UTC / 21:00 CEST / 3:00pm EDT (UTC -4)

Register: https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_JOqylCadQfGbcL_HsPoZoQ

The IDEAL program at the North Carolina Environmental Justice Network invites you to a webinar on Bringing Data Sovereignty into Participatory Sciences. Anna Woodroof, a researcher and program manager at IDEAL, will facilitate a conversation with Hali Dardar, a Houma scholar who created the Uke’ Contracting System for data sovereignty in the context of oral histories. We’ll also hear from Kurt Naquin, a Houma scholar, writer, and community-engaged researcher, and Caren Cooper, director of IDEAL and professor of public science. We will discuss data sovereignty and what might be possible by adapting the Uke’ system to the context of participatory science projects. We’ll explore what it could mean for individuals to retain ownership and control of their data while sharing those data with participatory projects for use and re-use. Registration is required. The guests will speak English. Live interpretation into Spanish and Portuguese will be available. Questions? Contact IDEAL@ncejn.org

title: Read Now – Disaster Risk Reduction and Open Data Newsletter: August 2026 Edition
content:
A data engineering approach to tracking global climate resilience

What counts as a climate-resilient road? One country might build to withstand a 1-in-50-year flood, another a 1-in-100-year flood, and both report against the same indicator. COP30 in Belém adopted 59 indicators for the Global Goal on Adaptation. Bapon Fakhruddin of the Green Climate Fund and Matti Heikkurinen of CODATA warn that figures which look comparable often are not. Their answer is not a single global standard but the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework, which acts as a translator between existing sectoral standards, so communities need not change how they collect data. Building it in from the outset costs far less than retrofitting it and decides whether the Global Stocktake measures genuine progress or merely records the attempt to describe it.

Energy strategy: The path for a prosperous, sustainable future
snippet: A data engineering approach to tracking global climate resilience

title: A data engineering approach to tracking global climate resilience
content:
An article illustrating the importance and benefits of the data engineering approach recommended by the WorldFAIR Policy Brief, was published on 19th August 2026 on the UNDRR’s PreventionWeb site.
 
‘A data engineering approach to tracking global climate resilience’ outlines the challenges related to developing consistent, efficient, and accurate methods for assessing the Belém indicators (adopted at the 30th United Nations Climate Change Conference in November 2025) for measuring progress towards climate resilience.  Also described are how the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF), the CDIF4EOSC project and other tools and methods supported by CODATA can help realise meet these challenges.

 
The article was written by Bapon Fakhruddin, co-chair of the CODATA FAIR Data for Disaster Risk Research Task Group, with input from Matti Heikkurinen, CODATA Project Portfolio Manager.

title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Open Data Newsletter: Jul 2026 Edition
content:
Release of the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) Version 1.1

The Committee on Data (CODATA) has released Version 1.1 of the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF), a practical framework that enables organisations across sectors to share and combine data without manual translation. Resulting from two years of implementation and development, including a disaster preparedness initiative in Malawi and implementation in the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) climate adaptation project (Climate-Adapt4EOSC), the release strengthens FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) data sharing. New features include standardised core data fields, improved packaging tools, and a developer toolkit, with future updates planned to enhance data quality, semantic mapping, and support for complex data and software resources.

Climate risk and disclosure in ports: Lessons from New Zealand and Australia

title: Crafting Participatory Tech Futures Online Workshops, 20 and 23 July!
content:
We would like to draw your attention to the Crafting Participatory Tech Futures Online Workshops which will be taking place on 20 and 23 July.

20 July, online (08:30-10:30 UTC): https://luma.com/1aa12iaw
23 July, online (16:30-18:30 UTC): https://luma.com/f30v8m09

​These are interactive, online workshops led by the Responsible Artificial Intelligence Network (RAIN), and invite civil society, academia and non-profits to affirm imagination as a collective practice.

What if AI futures were not something delivered to us, but something we could deliberate, contest, and build together? What if diverse publics could gather to imagine technological futures grounded in real societal and ecological needs, and chart practical pathways toward them?

​The workshops invite participants to affirm imagination as a collective practice. Through participatory world-building, we will move beyond abstract optimism or dystopian critique, and instead co-define actionable, justice-oriented AI futures.

​Discovery: Discover futures thinking as a critical practice that examines how imagined futures shape present decisions, power structures, and technological trajectories.

title: OntoPortal Workshop 2026: Exploring Semantic Technologies for Interoperable and FAIR Data
content:
The CDIF4EOSC, CDIF, CODATA and wider data stewardship communities are invited to participate in the public online session of the OntoPortal Workshop 2026, which will take place on 23 September 2026 from 14:00 to 17:00 CEST.

Register here!

The event is organised as part of the 5th OntoPortal Alliance Workshop, hosted by the Observatoire de Paris and coordinated by the OntoPortal-Astro team. It will bring together members of the OntoPortal Alliance, semantic technology experts, research infrastructures and data management practitioners to discuss recent developments and future directions in semantic interoperability.

The OntoPortal Alliance is an international consortium of research and infrastructure organisations that collaboratively develop and maintain the open-source OntoPortal software. The Alliance supports a growing ecosystem of semantic artefact catalogues and ontology repositories, including initiatives such as BioPortal, AgroPortal, EarthPortal, EcoPortal, BiodivPortal and OntoPortal-Astro.

title: Data policies for times of crisis: Enabling open science for coordinated response, UNESCO Global IDSSD Conference
content:
The UNESCO-CODATA WG on Data Policy for Times of Crisis invites participation in a session as part of the 2026 Global Conference of the International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development (IDSSD), 15-17 July 2026.

The session on Data policies for times of crisis: Enabling open science for coordinated response will take place in Room XI and online, on Friday 17 July at 12:30-13:45 UTC / 14:30-15:45 CEST (Local Time Paris)

Register to attend the Data Policities for Times of Crisis (DPTC) online!

Register to attend in person and to attend the Global Conference https://indico.un.org/event/1021402/

As crises become increasingly complex, interconnected, and transboundary, timely access to trustworthy data is essential for effective preparedness, response, and recovery. This event presents findings from the first global UNESCO-CODATA survey on the implementation of Data Policies for Times of Crisis (DPTC) facilitated by Open Science.
